claim: ATP synthases produce ATP by rotary catalysis, powered by the electrochemical proton gradient across the membrane.
source: ATP synthases produce ATP by rotary catalysis, powered by the electrochemical proton gradient across the membrane.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: The structure of an intact mitochondrial ATP synthase dimer was determined by electron cryo-microscopy at near-atomic resolution.
source: We determined the structure of an intact mitochondrial ATP synthase dimer by electron cryo-microscopy at near-atomic resolution.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental determination of the structure.

claim: Charged and polar residues of the a-subunit stator define two aqueous channels, each spanning one half of the membrane.
source: Charged and polar residues of the a-subunit stator define two aqueous channels, each spanning one half of the membrane.
evidence: This is directly observed in the structural data presented.

claim: The lumenal channel protonates an acidic glutamate in the c-ring rotor by passing through a conserved membrane-intrinsic helix hairpin.
source: Passing through a conserved membrane-intrinsic helix hairpin, the lumenal channel protonates an acidic glutamate in the c-ring rotor.
evidence: This mechanism is inferred from the structural arrangement observed in the cryo-EM map.

claim: Upon ring rotation, the protonated glutamate encounters the matrix channel and deprotonates.
source: Upon ring rotation, the protonated glutamate encounters the matrix channel and deprotonates.
evidence: This is a mechanistic inference based on the structural positions of channels and glutamate residues.

claim: An arginine between the two channels prevents proton leakage.
source: An arginine between the two channels prevents proton leakage.
evidence: This functional role is inferred from the position of aArg239 in the structure.

claim: The steep potential gradient over the sub-nm inter-channel distance exerts a force on the deprotonated glutamate, resulting in net directional rotation.
source: The steep potential gradient over the sub-nm inter-channel distance exerts a force on the deprotonated glutamate, resulting in net directional rotation.
evidence: This is a mechanistic inference based on the measured distances and calculated electrostatic fields.

claim: Mitochondrial ATP synthase uses the energy of the electrochemical proton gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane to produce ATP from ADP and phosphate by rotary catalysis.
source: Mitochondrial ATP synthase uses the energy of the electrochemical proton gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane to produce ATP from ADP and phosphate by rotary catalysis (Abrahams et al., 1994; Gresser et al., 1982).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: ATP synthases consist of the catalytic F1 head and the Fo subcomplex in the membrane.
source: ATP synthases consist of the catalytic F1 head and the Fo subcomplex in the membrane (von Ballmoos et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: Rotation is driven by protons flowing down the membrane gradient through the Fo subcomplex.
source: Rotation is driven by protons flowing down the membrane gradient through the Fo subcomplex.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: No high-resolution structure of an intact, functionally competent mitochondrial ATP synthase has been reported until now.
source: Until now, no high-resolution structure of an intact, functionally competent mitochondrial ATP synthase has been reported.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field prior to this work.

claim: The recent cryo-EM structure of the Fo subcomplex dimer isolated from yeast mitochondria indicated the positions of key residues in the proton pathway.
source: The recent cryo-EM structure of the Fo subcomplex dimer isolated from yeast mitochondria (Guo et al., 2017) indicated the positions of key residues in the proton pathway.
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: The structure of the complete mitochondrial ATP synthase dimer from the unicellular green alga Polytomella sp. was determined.
source: We have determined the structure of the complete mitochondrial ATP synthase dimer from the unicellular green alga Polytomella sp.
evidence: This is the main experimental result of the study.

claim: The structure reveals two prominent aqueous channels, each spanning one half of the membrane, that conduct protons to and from the conserved glutamates in the rotor ring.
source: Our structure reveals two prominent aqueous channels, each spanning one half of the membrane, that conduct protons to and from the conserved glutamates in the rotor ring.
evidence: This is directly observed in the structural data.

claim: Protonation and deprotonation of these glutamates drives ring rotation and ATP synthesis.
source: Protonation and deprotonation of these glutamates drives ring rotation and ATP synthesis.
evidence: This is a mechanistic inference based on the structural observations.

claim: Rotor rings of F-type ATP synthases consist of 8 to 15 identical c-subunits that each form a hydrophobic helix hairpin.
source: Rotor rings of F-type ATP synthases consist of 8 (Watt et al., 2010; Zhou et al., 2015) to 15 (Pogoryelov et al., 2009) identical c-subunits that each form a hydrophobic helix hairpin.
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: Mammalian mitochondria have a c8-ring.
source: Mammalian mitochondria have a c8-ring, while yeasts (Hahn et al., 2016; Stock et al., 1999) and Polytomella (Allegretti et al., 2015) have 10 c-ring subunits, which we refer to as cA to cJ.
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: Yeasts and Polytomella have 10 c-ring subunits.
source: Mammalian mitochondria have a c8-ring, while yeasts (Hahn et al., 2016; Stock et al., 1999) and Polytomella (Allegretti et al., 2015) have 10 c-ring subunits, which we refer to as cA to cJ.
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: A conserved glutamate (cGlu111 in Polytomella) serves as the c-subunit proton-binding site.
source: A conserved glutamate (cGlu111 in Polytomella) serves as the c-subunit proton-binding site (Meier et al., 2005; Pogoryelov et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: The previous 6.2 Å cryo-EM map of the Polytomella ATP synthase dimer indicated two long, membrane-intrinsic helix hairpins in subunit a, but did not resolve sidechains.
source: The previous 6.2 Å cryo-EM map of the Polytomella ATP synthase dimer indicated two long, membrane-intrinsic helix hairpins in subunit a (Allegretti et al., 2015), but did not resolve sidechains.
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: The helix hairpins run roughly at right angles to the c-ring helices.
source: The helix hairpins run roughly at right angles to the c-ring helices.
evidence: This is observed in the structural data.

claim: The longest helix bends around the c-ring, positioning the strictly conserved aArg239 and other key subunit a residues next to the c-subunit protonation site.
source: The longest helix bends around the c-ring, positioning the strictly conserved aArg239 and other key subunit a residues next to the c-subunit protonation site.
evidence: This is observed in the structural data.

claim: Subsequent structures of F-type and V-type ATPases at 3.7 to 7 Å resolution have shown that the long membrane-intrinsic helix hairpins are a conserved and apparently essential feature of all rotary ATPases.
source: Subsequent structures of F-type (Guo et al., 2017; Hahn et al., 2016; Morales-Rios et al., 2015) and V-type ATPases (Mazhab-Jafari et al., 2016) at 3.7 to 7 Å resolution have shown that the long membrane-intrinsic helix hairpins are a conserved and apparently essential feature of all rotary ATPases (Kühlbrandt and Davies, 2016), but the reason for this was not understood until now.
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: Two proton channels were proposed to provide access to the c-ring protonation sites.
source: Two proton channels were proposed to provide access to the c-ring protonation sites (Vik and Antonio, 1994) and first observed in the 6.2 Å Polytomella structure (Allegretti et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: The channels appear to be conserved in all rotary ATPases.
source: Like the a-subunit helix hairpins themselves, the channels appear to be conserved in all rotary ATPases (Kühlbrandt and Davies, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: Single-particle electron cryo-microscopy was performed on ATP synthase dimers of the colourless unicellular alga Polytomella sp.
source: We performed single-particle electron cryo-microscopy (cryo-EM) on ATP synthase dimers of the colourless unicellular alga Polytomella sp. to reveal the proton translocation pathway in atomic detail.
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: The Polytomella ATP synthase dimer has a molecular mass of ~1.6 MDa.
source: With a molecular mass of ~1.6 MDa and its bulky peripheral stalk of subunits ASA 1-9 (ATP synthase associated proteins 1–9) (Figure 1; Figure 1—figure supplement 1) (Vázquez-Acevedo et al., 2006), the robust, V-shaped Polytomella dimer is well suited to high-resolution cryo-EM.
evidence: This is a measured property of the complex.

claim: The Polytomella ATP synthase dimer has a bulky peripheral stalk of subunits ASA 1-9 (ATP synthase associated proteins 1–9).
source: With a molecular mass of ~1.6 MDa and its bulky peripheral stalk of subunits ASA 1-9 (ATP synthase associated proteins 1–9) (Figure 1; Figure 1—figure supplement 1) (Vázquez-Acevedo et al., 2006), the robust, V-shaped Polytomella dimer is well suited to high-resolution cryo-EM.
evidence: This is observed in the structural data and supported by a citation.

claim: The robust, V-shaped Polytomella dimer is well suited to high-resolution cryo-EM.
source: With a molecular mass of ~1.6 MDa and its bulky peripheral stalk of subunits ASA 1-9 (ATP synthase associated proteins 1–9) (Figure 1; Figure 1—figure supplement 1) (Vázquez-Acevedo et al., 2006), the robust, V-shaped Polytomella dimer is well suited to high-resolution cryo-EM.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural properties.

claim: A total of 90,142 particle images from 9,518 movies were aligned and refined to yield a map at 4.1 Å resolution.
source: A total of 90,142 particle images (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) from 9,518 movies recorded with a direct electron detector in counting mode were aligned and refined to yield a map at 4.1 Å resolution (Table 1; Figure 1—figure supplement 2B), in which most sidechains of the ~14,000 residue dimer are visible (Figure 1; Video 1), except in the F1 heads and central stalks, where blending of multiple rotational states reduces map definition.
evidence: This describes the data processing and resulting resolution.

claim: Most sidechains of the ~14,000 residue dimer are visible in the 4.1 Å resolution map, except in the F1 heads and central stalks, where blending of multiple rotational states reduces map definition.
source: A total of 90,142 particle images (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) from 9,518 movies recorded with a direct electron detector in counting mode were aligned and refined to yield a map at 4.1 Å resolution (Table 1; Figure 1—figure supplement 2B), in which most sidechains of the ~14,000 residue dimer are visible (Figure 1; Video 1), except in the F1 heads and central stalks, where blending of multiple rotational states reduces map definition.
evidence: This describes the quality of the structural data.

claim: Subvolume masking of the bulky peripheral stalk and associated Fo subunits improved the local resolution to 3.7 Å.
source: Subvolume masking of the bulky peripheral stalk and associated Fo subunits improved the local resolution to 3.7 Å (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This describes a data processing step and its result.

claim: The best-defined region of the assembly includes subunit a, the c-ring interface and ASA 6, which was built de novo.
source: The best-defined region of the assembly includes subunit a, the c-ring interface and ASA 6, which was built de novo (Figure 2; Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the quality of different regions in the structure.

claim: Sequences of functionally important subunit a regions are highly conserved and likely to have similar structures.
source: Sequences of functionally important subunit a regions are highly conserved (Figure 1—figure supplement 3) and likely to have similar structures.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and structural inference.

claim: In yeasts and mammals, subunit a is mitochondrially-encoded (known as ATP6 in human mitochondria).
source: In yeasts and mammals, subunit a is mitochondrially-encoded (known as ATP6 in human mitochondria), whereas in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii and, presumably, its close relative Polytomella, it is nuclear-encoded (Funes et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: In Chlamydomonas reinhardtii and, presumably, its close relative Polytomella, subunit a is nuclear-encoded.
source: In yeasts and mammals, subunit a is mitochondrially-encoded (known as ATP6 in human mitochondria), whereas in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii and, presumably, its close relative Polytomella, it is nuclear-encoded (Funes et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: N-terminal sequencing indicates that Polytomella subunit a has a 94-residue mitochondrial targeting sequence.
source: N-terminal sequencing indicates that Polytomella subunit a has a 94-residue mitochondrial targeting sequence (Vázquez-Acevedo et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: The polypeptide forms a total of six α-helices H1 to H6.
source: The polypeptide forms a total of six α-helices H1 to H6.
evidence: This is observed in the structural data.

claim: The mostly hydrophobic residues of the mature gene product are clearly resolved, except for the 11-residue loop connecting H4 and H5.
source: The mostly hydrophobic residues of the mature gene product are clearly resolved (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), except for the 11-residue loop connecting H4 and H5.
evidence: This describes the quality of the structural data.

claim: The N-terminal H1 on the matrix-facing membrane surface is amphipathic.
source: The N-terminal H1 on the matrix-facing membrane surface is amphipathic, whereas in fungal and mammalian a-subunits, the first helix crosses the membrane (Guo et al., 2017; Hahn et al., 2016; Zhou et al., 2015).
evidence: This is observed in the structural data.

claim: In fungal and mammalian a-subunits, the first helix crosses the membrane.
source: The N-terminal H1 on the matrix-facing membrane surface is amphipathic, whereas in fungal and mammalian a-subunits, the first helix crosses the membrane (Guo et al., 2017; Hahn et al., 2016; Zhou et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: The four-helix bundle of hairpins H3/H4 and H5/H6 is immersed in the hydrophobic membrane interior.
source: The four-helix bundle of hairpins H3/H4 and H5/H6 is immersed in the hydrophobic membrane interior.
evidence: This is observed in the structural data.

claim: The 52 residues of H5 include the essential aArg239 and seven other charged or polar sidechains, interspersed with hydrophobic residues in a striking, strongly conserved pattern.
source: The 52 residues of H5 include the essential (Mitome et al., 2010) aArg239 and seven other charged or polar sidechains, interspersed with hydrophobic residues in a striking, strongly conserved pattern (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is observed in the structural data and sequence analysis.

claim: The structure puts these residues into a functional context of proton translocation and force generation.
source: Our structure puts these residues into a functional context of proton translocation and force generation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural observations.

claim: Two prominent aqueous channels span half of the Fo assembly, one from each side of the membrane.
source: Two prominent aqueous channels span half of the Fo assembly, one from each side of the membrane (Figures 3,4).
evidence: This is observed in the structural data shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: The lumenal channel enables proton access to cGlu111 from the crista lumen.
source: The lumenal channel enables proton access to cGlu111 from the crista lumen.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural arrangement.

claim: The entrance of the lumenal channel is a 23 by 37 Å funnel between the c-ring, the loop connecting the membrane-intrinsic H3/H4 hairpin, and the two trans-membrane helices of subunit ASA 6.
source: Its entrance is a 23 by 37 Å funnel between the c-ring, the loop connecting the membrane-intrinsic H3/H4 hairpin, and the two trans-membrane helices of subunit ASA 6 (Figure 3A,C,D).
evidence: This is measured from the structural data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Although there is no detectable sequence homology, ASA 6 appears to take the place of the peripheral stalk subunit b in yeasts and mammals.
source: Although there is no detectable sequence homology, ASA 6 appears to take the place of the peripheral stalk subunit b in yeasts and mammals (Guo et al., 2017; Hahn et al., 2016; Zhou et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural comparison and cited references.

claim: Four lipid acyl chains and densities that accommodate two phosphatidyl head groups are resolved at the rim of the lumenal funnel, consistent with a cardiolipin molecule mediating close contacts between ASA 6 and subunit a in this position.
source: Four lipid acyl chains and densities that accommodate two phosphatidyl head groups are resolved at the rim of the lumenal funnel (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A), consistent with a cardiolipin molecule mediating close contacts between ASA 6 and subunit a in this position.
evidence: This is observed in the structural data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: In the protein interior, the lumenal channel is lined by conserved charged, polar and hydrophobic sidechains.
source: In the protein interior, the channel is lined by conserved charged, polar and hydrophobic sidechains (Figure 4; Figure 4—figure supplement 3A; Videos 2 and 3).
evidence: This is observed in the structural data shown in Figure 4 and supplementary figures.

claim: The lumenal channel extends to a cluster of buried, closely spaced glutamates and histidines (aGlu172, aHis248, aHis252, aGlu288) that appears to serve as a local reservoir for protons to be fed to the c-ring glutamates.
source: The lumenal channel extends to a cluster of buried, closely spaced glutamates and histidines (aGlu172, aHis248, aHis252, aGlu288; Figure 4A; Figure 5A; Videos 2 and 3) that appears to serve as a local reservoir for protons to be fed to the c-ring glutamates.
evidence: This is observed in the structural data and the functional role is inferred.

claim: At aGlu288 about 20 Å below the lumenal membrane surface, the channel narrows to 4 by 5 Å and changes direction by 90° towards the c-ring.
source: At aGlu288 about 20 Å below the lumenal membrane surface, the channel narrows to 4 by 5 Å and changes direction by 90° towards the c-ring (Figure 3D; Figure 4A).
evidence: This is measured from the structural data shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: In the hydrophobic membrane interior, the strictly conserved polar sidechains of aAsn243 (H5) and aGln295 (H6) that face one another would stabilise the H5/H6 hairpin.
source: In the hydrophobic membrane interior, the strictly conserved polar sidechains of aAsn243 (H5) and aGln295 (H6) that face one another would stabilise the H5/H6 hairpin (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is inferred from the structural arrangement shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The channel passes through the hairpin at the small, conserved sidechains of aAla246, aGly247 (H5) and aAla292 (H6).
source: The channel passes through the hairpin at the small, conserved sidechains of aAla246, aGly247 (H5) and aAla292 (H6) (Figure 3C,D; Figure 4A; Figure 5B; Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is observed in the structural data shown in multiple figures.

claim: Bulky hydrophobic sidechains close by on H5 and H6 keep the helices apart and the channel open.
source: Bulky hydrophobic sidechains close by on H5 and H6 keep the helices apart and the channel open (Figure 4A; Figure 5B).
evidence: This is inferred from the structural arrangement shown in Figures 4A and 5B.

claim: From aGlu288 the proton may jump to either of two c-ring glutamates.
source: From aGlu288 the proton may jump to either of two c-ring glutamates.
evidence: This is a mechanistic inference based on the structural positions.

claim: The path to cAGlu111 is 4 Å longer than the ~12 Å path to cBGlu111 but includes the hydrophilic sidechains of aAsn243 and cBSer112.
source: The path to cAGlu111 is 4 Å longer than the ~12 Å path to cBGlu111 (Figure 5C) but includes the hydrophilic sidechains of aAsn243 and cBSer112.
evidence: This is measured from the structural data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: In the static structure, the path to cAGlu111 is more favourable for proton transfer.
source: Therefore, in our static structure the path to cAGlu111 is more favourable for proton transfer.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural analysis.

claim: In a rotating c-ring, the estimated minimum distance from aGlu288 to cGlu111 is ~11 Å.
source: In a rotating c-ring, the estimated minimum distance from aGlu288 to cGlu111 is ~11 Å.
evidence: This is calculated from the structural data.

claim: These distance estimates are subject to an error margin of 3 to 4 Å, since the carboxyl groups of the glutamate sidechains are not visible in the map, as is usual in high-resolution cryo-EM structures due to radiation damage.
source: Note that these distance estimates are subject to an error margin of 3 to 4 Å, since the carboxyl groups of the glutamate sidechains are not visible in the map, as is usual in high-resolution cryo-EM structures due to radiation damage (Allegretti et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a limitation of the technique, supported by a cited reference.

claim: The strictly conserved aArg239 is positioned halfway between the matrix and lumenal channels, forming a positively charged seal that prevents proton leakage from the lumen to the matrix.
source: The strictly conserved aArg239 is positioned halfway between the matrix and lumenal channels (Figures 3A–C,4; Video 2), forming a positively charged seal that prevents proton leakage from the lumen to the matrix.
evidence: This is observed in the structural data and the functional role is inferred.

claim: The map density for aArg239 sidechain is particularly well defined.
source: The map density for this arginine sidechain is particularly well defined (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is observed in the structural data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The position and orientation of aArg239 do not suggest a salt bridge with the deprotonated c-ring glutamate, which would impede ring rotation.
source: Its position and orientation do not suggest a salt bridge with the deprotonated c-ring glutamate, which would impede ring rotation.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural arrangement.

claim: aAsn243, cSer112, the protonated cGlu111 and the two aqueous channels provide a local hydrophilic environment.
source: aAsn243, cSer112, the protonated cGlu111 and the two aqueous channels provide a local hydrophilic environment.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural arrangement.

claim: The shortest distance between the lumenal and matrix channels on either side of aArg239 is ~6 Å.
source: The shortest distance between the lumenal and matrix channels on either side of aArg239 is ~6 Å.
evidence: This is measured from the structural data.

claim: The matrix channel is defined by the N-terminal half of H5 (residues 221–239), the C-terminal half of H6 (301–312) and residues cTyr102 to cGlu111 of the outer helices of c-subunits A and J.
source: The matrix channel (Figure 3B,C,E, 4C; Figure 4—figure supplement 3B; Videos 2 and 4) is defined by the N-terminal half of H5 (residues 221–239), the C-terminal half of H6 (301–312) and residues cTyr102 to cGlu111 of the outer helices of c-subunits A and J.
evidence: This is observed in the structural data shown in multiple figures.

claim: The deepest point of the matrix channel is a 4 Å by 7 Å cavity next to cJGlu111, ~25 Å below the c-ring surface.
source: Its deepest point is a 4 Å by 7 Å cavity next to cJGlu111, ~25 Å below the c-ring surface.
evidence: This is measured from the structural data.

claim: The matrix channel widens to 7 by 13 Å at aArg232 (H5) and cJLeu104 and continues straight to the 36 by 30 Å exit funnel on the matrix side.
source: The channel widens to 7 by 13 Å at aArg232 (H5) and cJLeu104 and continues straight to the 36 by 30 Å exit funnel on the matrix side.
evidence: This is measured from the structural data.

claim: H4 and H5 describe two sides of a triangle that is wedged open by the conserved aromatic sidechains of aTrp189 (H4) and aTyr229 (H5), which forms a hydrogen bond to aThr193 (H4).
source: H4 and H5 describe two sides of a triangle that is wedged open by the conserved aromatic sidechains of aTrp189 (H4) and aTyr229 (H5), which forms a hydrogen bond to aThr193 (H4) (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is observed in the structural data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The aromatic wedge of aTrp189 and aTyr229 induces a change in direction of H5 to follow the curvature of the c-ring.
source: The aromatic wedge of aTrp189 and aTyr229 induces a change in direction of H5 to follow the curvature of the c-ring.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural arrangement.

claim: Like the lumenal channel, the matrix channel includes conserved charged and polar sidechains, notably aGlu225 (H5) and aGlu309 (H6), which form a salt bridge with aArg232 (H5).
source: Like the lumenal channel, the matrix channel includes conserved charged and polar sidechains (Figure 4C; Figure 1—figure supplement 3; Figure 4—figure supplement 3B), notably aGlu225 (H5) and aGlu309 (H6), which form a salt bridge with aArg232 (H5).
evidence: This is observed in the structural data shown in multiple figures.

claim: At a distance of 7.4 Å, aGlu225 is in a good position to receive protons from cGlu111.
source: At a distance of 7.4 Å, aGlu225 is in a good position to receive protons from cGlu111.
evidence: This is measured from the structural data and the functional role is inferred.

claim: The protons pass via aGlu309 and aHis312 near the channel exit into the matrix.
source: The protons pass via aGlu309 and aHis312 near the channel exit into the matrix.
evidence: This is a mechanistic inference based on the structural arrangement.

claim: The relevance of residues at the matrix channel to human health is highlighted by a number of mutations in ATP6, the a-subunit of human ATP synthase, that result in severe and, at present, incurable diseases.
source: The relevance of residues at the matrix channel to human health is highlighted by a number of mutations in ATP6, the a-subunit of human ATP synthase, that result in severe and, at present, incurable diseases.
evidence: This is supported by the disease-related mutations discussed in the text.

claim: Several disease-related mutations in ATP6 map to H4, H5 and H6.
source: Several of these mutations map to H4, H5 and H6 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Sequence comparison indicates that functionally important subunit a residues are conserved in ATP6.
source: Sequence comparison (Figure 1—figure supplement 3) indicates that functionally important subunit a residues are conserved in ATP6.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: A change of atp6Leu156 (aLeu236 in Polytomella) to Arg or Pro reduces ATP production by 70%.
source: A change of atp6Leu156 (aLeu236 in Polytomella) to Arg or Pro reduces ATP production by 70%.
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: Mutations of atp6Leu156 to Arg or Pro result in Maternally Inherited Leigh Syndrome (MILS) or in Neuropathy, Ataxia and Retinitis Pigmentosa (NARP) Syndrome.
source: Both mutations result in Maternally Inherited Leigh Syndrome (MILS) or in Neuropathy, Ataxia and Retinitis Pigmentosa (NARP) Syndrome (Cortés-Hernández et al., 2007; Holt et al., 1990; Kucharczyk et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: aLeu236 marks the point where H5 bends around the c-ring.
source: aLeu236 marks the point where H5 bends around the c-ring.
evidence: This is observed in the structural data.

claim: A change of the nearby Trp (aTrp189 in Polytomella) in H4 to arginine causes Bilateral Striatal Lesions.
source: A change of the nearby Trp (aTrp189 in Polytomella) in H4 to arginine causes Bilateral Striatal Lesions (De Meirleir et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: aTrp189 appears to be crucial for keeping H4, H5 and H6 apart and the matrix channel open.
source: aTrp189 appears to be crucial for keeping H4, H5 and H6 apart and the matrix channel open.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural arrangement.

claim: Replacing these residues by an arginine or proline would disrupt the interaction of H5 with the c-ring rotor, impairing proton translocation and ATP synthesis.
source: Replacing these residues by an arginine or proline would disrupt the interaction of H5 with the c-ring rotor, impairing proton translocation and ATP synthesis.
evidence: This is a mechanistic inference based on the structural observations.

claim: Mutations of atp6Leu217, atp6Leu220 and atp6Leu222 (aLeu302, aVal305 and aVal307 in Polytomella) on H6 result in Leigh Syndrome and reduced ATPase activity.
source: Mutations of atp6Leu217, atp6Leu220 and atp6Leu222 (aLeu302, aVal305 and aVal307 in Polytomella) on H6 in the same region of the long helix hairpin also result in Leigh Syndrome and reduced ATPase activity (Castagna et al., 2007; Moslemi et al., 2005; Thyagarajan et al., 1995) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: The structure provides direct new insights into the cause of serious mitochondrial diseases.
source: Our structure thus provides direct new insights into the cause of serious mitochondrial diseases.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural analysis of disease-related mutations.

claim: Rotation of the c-ring is driven by the proton-motive force (pmf) across the inner mitochondrial membrane, which has a chemical component (ΔpH ≅ 0.8 units, equivalent to ~50 mV) and an electrostatic component (ΔΨ ≅ 150 mV).
source: Rotation of the c-ring is driven by the proton-motive force (pmf) across the inner mitochondrial membrane, which has a chemical component (ΔpH ≅ 0.8 units, equivalent to ~50 mV) and an electrostatic component (ΔΨ ≅ 150 mV).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: The higher concentration of protons acts to protonate c-subunit A in the lumenal channel.
source: The higher concentration of protons acts to protonate c-subunit A in the lumenal channel, whereas in the matrix channel, the incoming protonated c-subunit J would lose its proton to the pH 8 matrix (Figure 3A,B; Figure 6; Video 2).
evidence: This is a mechanistic inference based on the structural arrangement and pH gradient.

claim: In the matrix channel, the incoming protonated c-subunit J would lose its proton to the pH 8 matrix.
source: The higher concentration of protons acts to protonate c-subunit A in the lumenal channel, whereas in the matrix channel, the incoming protonated c-subunit J would lose its proton to the pH 8 matrix (Figure 3A,B; Figure 6; Video 2).
evidence: This is a mechanistic inference based on the structural arrangement and pH gradient.

claim: Protonation in the lumenal channel neutralises the residue and favours the buried sidechain conformation observed in x-ray structures of isolated c-rings.
source: Protonation in the lumenal channel neutralises the residue and favours the buried sidechain conformation observed in x-ray structures of isolated c-rings (Pogoryelov et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: Protonation would allow c-subunit A to move to position B, where it partitions into the hydrophobic environment of the membrane by counter-clockwise rotation, as seen from the matrix.
